QF.id: VB Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_12

question.text: What is the minimum amount required to start investing in most mutual fund SIPs (Systematic Investment Plans)?

answer.text: As low as Rs. 500 per month

explanation.text: The Logic: SIPs are designed to allow investors to participate in mutual funds through small periodic contributions rather than large lump sums. As a general industry norm in India, most mutual fund schemes accept SIPs starting at very small amounts — commonly as low as Rs. 500 per month — which makes mutual funds accessible across income levels. The Trap: Options B and D suggest large monthly amounts (Rs. 50,000 or Rs. 10,000), which would defeat the small-ticket philosophy of SIPs. Option C describes a lump-sum threshold (Rs. 1,00,000 one-time), not a SIP minimum. Note: The cited NISM Series V-B workbook supports the broader point that SIPs require smaller periodic amounts than lump-sum purchases and that schemes specify the minimum investment for each tranche, but the specific 'Rs. 500 per month' SIP minimum was not located in the pages reviewed. The figure above reflects common industry practice across Indian mutual funds rather than a direct workbook citation.
